entities.summary: Jean I Le Meingre, also known as Boucicaut, was a 14th century French noble who rose to prominence as Marshal of France. Born into the noble class, Le Meingre's family had a long history of military service and public office. He entered the service of King Philip VI of Valois at a young age and quickly distinguished himself as a skilled military commander. Le Meingre played a key role in several battles, including the Battle of Agincourt and the Battle of Poitiers, where he captured the English King Edward III. His military successes and strategic alliances helped to establish him as one of the most influential figures of his time. Le Meingre's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he also played a significant role in shaping the politics and governance of France during the late Middle Ages. He died in 1367, leaving behind a legacy that continues to be studied by historians today. Le Meingre's story is a testament to the enduring power of family, duty, and loyalty in shaping the course of history. He remains an important figure in French history, a reminder of the complexities and nuances of medieval politics and society.
